# DB — NEW Schema (Supabase + Drizzle)

Design targets (from plan): thread === workflow (1:1 after bind), chat-first,
PERSONAL auto workspace, MVP single-workspace (scalable), durable chat + queued
messages, binding approvals, plans with steps, activities/tool streaming for
ThinkingSteps, per-workspace API keys, mem0 thread memory, files in Supabase
Storage, realtime notifications, **collaboration** (workspace membership +
thread sharing, see ARCHITECTURE §I Permission model).

## Conventions
- Every table: `id text primary key` (ULID via `packages/db/src/ids.ts`,
  prefixes `thd_`, `wf_`, `msg_`, `run_`, `pln_`, `pls_`, `apv_`, `not_`, `key_`,
  `fil_`, `wp_`, `grp_`, `inv_`, `tco_`, `wme_`, `alm_`), `created_at timestamptz not null default
  now()`, `updated_at`.
- All plaintext user data (API keys, secrets) NEVER stored — use Supabase Vault
  or encrypted column (see `workspace_api_keys`).
- RLS on every user table: `to authenticated using ( owner = auth.uid() )`
  (+ `with check` on update). Owner column is almost always `user_id`.
- text enums via Postgres `enum` types; drizzle maps to TS unions.

| path | text not null | storage path `{user}/{thread}/{ulid}.ext` |
| mime_type | text |
| size_bytes | bigint |
| compressed | bool default false |
| created_at |
RLS: owner. Storage bucket policy: authenticate (owner by path prefix `{auth.uid()}/`).

### 17. `notification_webhooks` (optional future) — REMOVED from MVP, note only.
External webhooks folded into `notifications` + Inngest `notification/publish`,
existing `webhook-board`/`waitForWebhook` retired.

## Enums (Postgres)
```
role            : owner|editor|viewer          (workspace_members)
thread_role     : editor|viewer                (thread_shares / invites; no owner row — owner = threads.user_id)
plan            : free|pro
group_kind      : custom|system
invite_kind     : workspace|thread
invite_status   : pending|accepted|revoked|expired
workflow_status : waiting|planning|running|awaiting_approval|idle|paused|failed|completed
message_role    : user|assistant|system|tool
message_status  : queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted
run_status      : pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled
activity_status : pending|active|complete|failed
activity_type   : tool|thinking|task|subtask|system
approval_status : pending|approved|denied
api_provider    : groq|anakin|mem0|image|speech|transcription|video
```

## Supabase specifics
- Migrations via `supabase migration new <name>` (imperative workflow).
- **Realtime**: enable on `chat_messages`, `run_activities`,
  `approval_requests`, `notifications` with private channels + JWT auth.
- **Storage bucket**: `chat-attachments` — create server-side w/ service role;
  dedicated policy `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text` for
  CUD. Policy for avatar/object keys too.
- **RLS policy list**:
  - owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys,
    files (+ own invites).
  - workspace-scoped: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans,
    chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner
    OR any `workspace_members` row (all threads visible to members).
  - cross-workspace thread access: `threads` also readable via a matching
    `thread_shares` row (invitee; in their OWN workspace context / INVITES
    group). Never bundled into a shared-workspace read.
  - `workspace_api_keys`: SELECT only via `security definer` RPC
    `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` that validates <owner OR
    workspace_members> and decrypts server-side (service role decrypt NOT
    exposed). Member key resolution honors `user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared`
    → falls back to the member's OWN Personal workspace keys.
- **Oracle triggers**: `on_auth_user_created` → insert
  `workspaces(Personal)` (is_default) + `user_profiles` row +
  `workspace_members(owner)` for that workspace + system `groups`
  (PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES — INVITES locked empty) automatically.

## Why this shape (reasoning)
- `threads` + `workflows` split: a chat exists before any plan/bind; binding
  sets `threads.bound_workflow_id`. MVP single-workspace but multi-thread.
- `groups` = the sidebar folder concept the plan asks for (New button → new
  custom group; INVITES is a LOCKED system group created at signup — empty
  until a thread invite is accepted). Group/thread limits (≤5 threads/group,
  ≤3 custom groups/workspace free) enforced at insert.
- `invites` unified (workspace | thread) keeps one token/status/expiry flow;
  accept fans out to `workspace_members` or `thread_shares`.
- `thread_shares` = invited guests only; role editor/viewer — guests get chat/
  run/approve but never plan-edit/rename/re-share (owner-only rights stay on
  `threads.user_id`).
- `runs` separate from workflow status: each durable pass is auditable,
  replayable, cancellable; activity tables hang off `run_id`.
- `run_activities` replaces old `event`/`observation`/`agent_state` — shaped
  directly for the ThinkingSteps/ToolStep UI components and realtime push,
  killing the god-table smell.
- `chat_messages` owns history (requirement: no hardcoded mock); queue solved
  by `status=queued` rows — durable across page close/reload.
- Plain user-supplied keys isolated in ONE table (never in env, never client)
  → the "Agent/Environment" dialog writes here.

migration file to snapshot it, THEN write the brand-new schema. This doc is the
old-schema snapshot + the migration roadmap.

## Step 0 — Current state facts
- Drizzle + `pg` (node-postgres), config: `packages/db/drizzle.config.ts`,
  dataload from `apps/web/.env`.
- `packages/db/src/migrations/` contains ONLY `.gitkeep` — no SQL generated yet.
- Supabase local scaffold exists (`packages/db/supabase/config.toml`,

- Old auth = better-auth (tables user/session/account/verification) → to be
  REPLACED by Supabase Auth (Google-only for MVP).
- `scripts/reset.ts` truncates 11 domain tables (workflow, workflow_execution,
  workflow_step, tool_execution, agent_state, event, observation,
  recovery_attempt, schedule, notification, approval).

## Step 1 — Snapshot the OLD schema (the migration ask)

Generate the migration that captures the CURRENT tables, so the redesign result
is compared against it. Use drizzle-kit to produce an initial migration file.

Existing 14 tables (from `src/schema/`, id prefix in `src/ids.ts`):

1. `user` (better-auth) — id, name, email, emailVerified, image, createdAt, updatedAt
2. `session` (better-auth) — id, userId→user(CASCADE), token?, expiresAt, createdAt, updatedAt
3. `account` (better-auth) — id, userId→user(CASCADE), accountId, providerId, **accessToken, refreshToken** (plaintext), expiresAt, password, createdAt, updatedAt
4. `verification` (better-auth) — id, identifier, value, expiresAt, createdAt
5. `workflow` — id(wf_), userId→user, objective, status (9 states), schemaVersion, archivedAt, createdAt, updatedAt
6. `workflow_execution` — id(exe_), workflowId→workflow, status (8 states), reason, prompt, costUsd, tokenCount
7. `workflow_step` — id(step_), workflowId→workflow, executionId, kind, assistantText, status, order, idempotencyKey
8. `tool_execution` — id(tool_), workflowId, executionId (set null), stepId (set null), order, tool, provider, status, input jsonb, output jsonb, errorCode, durationMs
9. `agent_state` — id(agent_state_), workflowId, phase, status, version (optimistic), data jsonb
10. `approval` — id(ap_), workflowId, executionId (CASCADE), userId, toolName, input, status (pending), reason, decidedAt
11. `event` — id(evt_), workflowId (CASCADE), executionId (set null), type, data jsonb, occurredAt
12. `notification` — id(ntf_), userId, workflowId (set null), type, channel, subject, body, deliveredAt, readAt
13. `observation` — id(obs_), workflowId, type, content jsonb, observedAt
14. `recovery_attempt` — id(rec_), workflowId, executionId, failureClass, failureCode, attempt, strategy, result, detail, completedAt
15. `schedule` — id(sched_), workflowId, cron, intervalSeconds, nextRunAt, lastRunAt, enabled, config
16. `webhook_board` — id(whk_), tokenHash (unique), instruction, status, expiresAt, usedAt

> Better-auth `account.access_token`/`refresh_token` + `password` live in
> plaintext columns — snapshot then DROP with the auth tables.

**Command**: `bun db:generate` (turbo `-F @aevryn/db`) with migrations out dir.
Commit this as `001_old_schema_snapshot.sql` in a `migrations/` folder.

## Step 2 — Unexpected-but-simple wins (kill in snapshot while migrating)
- Delete better-auth 4 tables (auth moves to Supabase Auth).
- Delete `webhook_board` (replaced by in-app webhooks via Supabase Realtime +
  RPC; MVP doesn't need external token hooks).
- Delete `agent_state`, `recovery_attempt`, `event`, `observation` (the new
  schema folds activity into different tables; see SCHEMA.md).

## Step 3 — Supabase-init
- `supabase init` already done (`config.toml`). Set `schema_paths`, add
  `seed.sql` (insert PERSONAL workspace for new users via a trigger instead —
  prefer DB trigger → no seed file needed).
- Auth providers: enable Google (`[auth.external.google] enabled = true`,
  create provider in Supabase dashboard with Google OAuth app).
- Realtime: enable `wal_level=logical` for Postgres → Realtime broadcasts.

## Step 4 — Orders of tables (all `create index ... if not exists`)
See SCHEMA.md for full DDL roadmap. Create order:
1. identity/auth users (`auth.users` exists) → 2. workspaces →
3. groups (PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS/CUSTOM) → 4. workspace_members (owner/editor/viewer) →
5. profiles (incl. prefer_own_keys_in_shared) → 6. threads (group_id, share_enabled) →
7. workflows (bound to threads) → 8. chat_messages → 9. runs / run_activities →
10. plans + plan_steps → 11. approval_requests → 12. invites (workspace|thread) →
13. thread_shares (shows under INVITES system group) → 14. notifications →
15. workspace_api_keys → 16. files.
RLS: owner OR workspace_members read on workspace-scoped tables; `thread_shares`
grants cross-workspace thread read to the guest.

## Guardrails
- Run `supabase db advisors` after migration; fix issues before proceeding
  (supabase skill requirement).
- RLS on EVERY table (`TO authenticated` + owner predicate `using/auth.uid()`).
- Keep `drizzle-kit` as tool, but treat Supabase as source of truth; generate
  drizzle migration only when required for type-check parity.

- `apps/web/.env` has DATABASE_URL, DIRECT_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (values unknown/untouched — I won't print them).

- The old db package used: drizzle-orm, pg, postgres, dotenv, zod, ulid; devDeps drizzle-kit, @types/pg, typescript. Also depended on @aevryn/env. And there was a `scripts/reset.ts`.
- Old tsconfig used composite + declaration. 
- config.toml: baseline exists. I need to enable Google external auth for P1 later — but that's commit 4/5 (auth). For commit 3 I can enable Google provider + keep seed disabled (already done) + adjust site_url? The site_url says 127.0.0.1:3000 but apps/web runs on port 3001 (`next dev --port 3001`)! So auth redirects would need 3001. But that's P1/P5 territory. For commit 3 I'll set site_url to http://127.0.0.1:3001 to match dev port, and enable google external. Also supabase on this repo: note `project_id = "db"`.

Now, about the supabase migrations location: `packages/db/supabase/`. supabase CLI works from the dir containing `supabase/`. So user would run commands from `packages/db/`. Fine, docs it.

Now, the PLAN P2: "supabase migration new new_schema". I'll hand-write the SQL file with a timestamped name `20260911XXXXXX_new_schema.sql`.

**Critical design work — the schema.** Let me carefully design the drizzle schema + SQL so they match perfectly. I must be meticulous given the user "struggled in db schema changes." Let me plan the 17 tables + all enums + RLS + triggers + realtime + storage.

Enums (from SCHEMA.md):
```
role            : owner|editor|viewer          (workspace_members)
thread_role     : editor|viewer                (thread_shares / invites)
plan            : free|pro
group_kind      : custom|system
invite_kind     : workspace|thread
invite_status   : pending|accepted|revoked|expired
workflow_status : waiting|planning|running|awaiting_approval|idle|paused|failed|completed
message_role    : user|assistant|system|tool
message_status  : queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted
run_status      : pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled
activity_status : pending|active|complete|failed
activity_type   : tool|thinking|task|subtask|system
approval_status : pending|approved|denied
api_provider    : groq|anakin|mem0|image|speech|transcription|video
```
Plus more enums from table docs:
- plan_status: draft|proposed|accepted|declined (plans table)
- plan_step_status: pending|active|completed|skipped (plan_steps)
- run_trigger: message|schedule|resume|approval|rerun (runs)
- run activity detail note
- notification_type: system|workflow|run|security|webhook (notifications)
- invite role enum: editor|viewer → that's thread_role
- file — no enum

IDs required check (ID_PREFIXES from SCHEMA.md conventions): thd_ (threads), wf_ (workflows), msg_ (chat_messages), run_ (runs), pln_ (plans), pls_ (plan_steps), apv_ (approval_requests), not_ (notifications), key_ (workspace_api_keys), fil_ (files), wp_ (workspaces), grp_ (groups), inv_ (invites), tco_ (thread_shares), wme_ (workspace_members), prf_ (user_profiles). Also run_activities = act_. So ID_PREFIXES should include: workspace "wp_", group "grp_", workspaceMember "wme_", profile "prf_", thread "thd_", workflow "wf_", plan "pln_", planStep "pls_", chatMessage "msg_", run "run_", activity "act_", approval "apv_", invite "inv_", threadShare "tco_", notification "not_", workspaceApiKey "key_", file "fil_".

The `alm_` prefix in SCHEMA.md line 13 doesn't map to any table (maybe an earlier idea for... alarm/schedule?). Skip: no schedule table exists in the new schema (schedules folded into runs + Inngest cron). I'll drop alm_.

**Enums and the `message_status`**: SCHEMA.md lists `queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted`. The table doc for chat_messages also mentions `draft` status. The enum block at bottom says `message_status : queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted` (no draft). But table 8 notes: `status | enum(draft, queued, streaming, completed, failed, interrupted)`. Conflict! The table doc includes `draft`. The user plan says "ChatComposer reads DB queue". The final enum list omits draft. Hmm. Two authoritative spots disagree. I'll include `draft` (table doc is more specific & detailed; the summary enum block is abbreviated). Actually wait — let me re-read the summary: `message_status  : queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted`. And table: `enum(draft, queued, streaming, completed, failed, interrupted)`. I'll include "draft" since the field-level doc explicitly lists it and it's useful (in-progress composer messages persisted? Not necessarily). Hmm, to be safe and consistent with the table doc which is the fuller spec — include draft. I'll note the discrepancy in my reasoning to the user.

**Table-by-table design** (from SCHEMA.md). Let me define each.

Conventions: `id text primary key`, `created_at timestamptz not null default now()`, `updated_at timestamptz not null default now()`. user_id columns are UUID (auth.users). 

**1. workspaces** — id wp_, name text not null, created_by uuid not null ref auth.users, is_default bool not null default false, created_at, updated_at. Unique(created_by, name). RLS owner only.

**2. groups** — id grp_, workspace_id text ref workspaces cascade, user_id uuid ref auth.users (creator), name text not null, kind group_kind default custom, position int default 0, created_at, updated_at. Unique(workspace_id, name). Index (workspace_id, position). RLS owner OR member read; owner/member CUD. Actually "RLS: owner OR member. Readable to user when owner or workspace member." For writes: creator can edit; workspace owner manages. Simplify: SELECT using owner OR member; INSERT with check owner OR member; UPDATE/DELETE using (workspace owner OR user_id=current) ... Let me keep it clean: 
- SELECT: `(workspace.owner = uid) OR (workspace_members exists)` → but that's a join over workspace/workspace_members. In RLS we reference other tables with EXISTS.
- Actually for `groups`, `threads`, `workflows`, `plans/plan_steps`, `chat_messages`, `runs`, `run_activities`, `approval_requests`, workspace members can see everything (all threads visible to members). Guests via thread_shares: only see specific shared thread's chat_messages/runs/run_activities/approval_requests and that thread row itself.
- For mutations: editor can create/edit/delete ANY thread+group. viewer read-only. Owner everything.

RLS policy design needs care. Let me define helper functions in SQL:
- `is_workspace_owner(ws_id)` = exists workspace_members where workspace_id=ws_id and user_id=uid and role='owner'
- `is_workspace_member(ws_id)` = exists workspace_members where workspace_id=ws_id and user_id=uid
- `is_workspace_editor(ws_id)` = member with role in ('owner','editor')
- `is_thread_owner(thread_id)` = exists threads.id=thread_id and user_id=uid
- `is_thread_guest(thread_id)` = exists thread_shares where thread_id and user_id=uid
- `can_read_thread(thd)` = is_thread_owner OR is_workspace_member(thread.workspace_id) OR is_thread_guest

Careful about RLS recursion: helper functions must be `security definer`? No — plain functions referencing tables that have RLS will (in PG 15+) run with the caller's permission? Actually, by default, functions run as the invoking user's permissions, and if SECURITY INVOKER with RLS tables, then RLS applies. That causes infinite recursion risk: an RLS policy on threads calls fn that queries threads → nested RLS → could recurse. Solution: mark helper functions `security definer` with `search_path` set to public, revoke from public, grant to authenticated + service_role. Security definer bypasses RLS (runs as owner). This is the standard Supabase pattern (like `is_claims_admin`). I'll mark helpers SECURITY DEFINER, set `SET search_path = public, pg_temp`.

Since the schema is largely deterministic, let me now also think about limits triggers:
- `enforce_group_limit`: when inserting a custom group, check count of custom groups in that workspace < 3 (free plan). Also INVITES is system/locked: 
  - prevent rename/delete of system groups: trigger forbids UPDATE name on kind='system' and forbids DELETE on kind='system'. 
- `enforce_thread_limit`: at most 5 threads per group (count threads where group_id = new.group_id and deleted_at is null) — and/or per workspace. Doc says ≤5 threads/group, ≤3 groups/workspace free. Enforced at insert.
- Invites to INVITES group only on accept — the accept RPC will place the shared thread under the INVITES system group for the guest. But wait — thread sharing places the SAME thread into the guest's sidebar under INVITES group, but the thread has a single group_id (owner's group). How does the guest see it under their own INVITES group? Hmm. The thread belongs to owner's workspace + owner's group. The guest's view of the thread under INVITES is a *view* concern, not a group_id change (can't have two groups per thread). 

This is subtle. SCHEMA doesn't have a junction table for guest→group placement. The guests see the thread "under their INVITES system group" — but implementation-wise that's the guest's UI grouping when the thread's workspace_id != guest's personal workspace. i.e., when rendering sidebar for a user, threads they can see that belong to THEIR personal workspace get grouped by group_id; threads from elsewhere (via thread_shares) get shown under the INVITES system group of their Personal workspace. So the INVITES group is essentially the bucket for cross-workspace shared threads. OK — so no DB column needed; the UI decides. Good, that matches "no additional table". I'll document that in a comment... no wait, no docstrings in code per user rule. I'll put rationale in SQL comments? User said "No docstrings in code." SQL comments are fine and valuable for schema maintainers, but the rule says no docstrings — I'll keep SQL comments minimal but present for triggers (SQL isn't TS code and the supabase-postgres skill encourages comments where non-obvious). Actually rule number: "No docstrings in code. No hardcoding." I'll avoid excessive comments; keep short ones where clarity matters.

- `on_auth_user_created()`: creates Personal workspace (name 'Personal', is_default=true, created_by=new.id), inserts user_profiles (onboarded=false), inserts workspace_members (role owner), creates system groups PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES (kind system) for that workspace. INVITES locked empty.

Realtime: `alter publication supabase_realtime add table public.chat_messages, public.run_activities, public.approval_requests, public.notifications;`

Storage bucket `chat-attachments`: `insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public) values ('chat-attachments','chat-attachments', false);` + storage.objects policies: owner by path prefix `{auth.uid()}`.

Also need `get_workspace_key` RPC (security definer) to read workspace_api_keys masking: validates owner OR member, returns decrypted key. But keys stored in `key_encrypted bytea` with AES-256-GCM using `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. For MVP commit 3, define the column + RPC stub returning masked or actual. Actually ENV.md: "Recommend Supabase Vault — no extra env key." But SCHEMA.md table 15 says `key_encrypted bytea not null` AES-256-GCM or Vault. The OBSERVATION recounted that the deleted rebuild had `bytea` customType. I'll keep `key_encrypted bytea` + `iv bytea`? AES-256-GCM needs nonce/iv. Simplest robust design: store `key_ciphertext bytea` + `key_iv bytea`? Or use Vault. For commit 3 I keep schema simple: columns `key_encrypted bytea not null`. The RPC `get_workspace_key` will return the raw bytea and the service layer decrypts server-side; but raw bytea select on RLS owner-only is fine. Hmm, the doc says RPC validates <owner OR workspace_members> and decrypts server-side. If we use Vault, we'd store via vault.create_secret. Given commit 3 scope, I'll:
- Table `workspace_api_keys`: provider api_provider, key_encrypted bytea not null, key_iv bytea not null, model_name text null. (AES-256-GCM params: 12-byte iv.)
- RPC `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` security definer: returns masked? Actually for server-side use it must return the real key to the server (which then uses it). But RPC called from client could leak. The doc: "SELECT only via security definer RPC get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider) that validates <owner OR workspace_members> and decrypts server-side (service role decrypt NOT exposed)." The service_role can call it from server. For commit 3 I'll implement the RPC to return the key bytes + model_name, restricted to owner/member, and encrypt/decrypt helpers (`set_workspace_key` / `get_workspace_key`) as security definer functions using pgcrypto with APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY via... hmm, pgp_sym_encrypt/decrypt with a key. Where does the key come from? Supabase Vault better. But Vault secrets are per-project. 

This is getting deep. For commit 3 (schema foundation), I'll implement encryption helpers using pgcrypto `pgp_sym_encrypt/decrypt` with a config param defaulting to the project's `vault` if available... Actually cleanest MVP that satisfies "no plaintext": use Supabase Vault `vault.create_secret` on write via a helper RPC `save_workspace_key`, and `decrypted_secrets` read via `get_workspace_key` RPC. But Vault requires the vault schema extension — `supabase start` includes Vault? The Vault extension (`vault` schema) ships with Supabase (decrypted_secrets view etc.) only when enabled. It's available in cloud; locally need `create extension if not exists vault with schema extensions;`? Actually Supabase's provided vault extension is preinstalled on cloud projects; locally it may need enabling. To avoid overcomplicating commit 3, I'll implement pgcrypto-based helpers (extension pgcrypto is always available) with a column `key_encrypted bytea` + `key_iv bytea`, functions `save_workspace_key` + `get_workspace_key` using a key derived from... server env can't reach DB funcs easily except via config. 

Note AES key management needs APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY. ENV.md says "or Supabase Vault if service_role available. Recommend Supabase Vault — no extra env key". So pivot to Vault: store via `vault.create_secret(secret, name)`, unique name = `wk:{workspace_id}:{provider}`. But then the table `workspace_api_keys` becomes metadata-only (no secret column) and vault holds it. However SCHEMA.md explicitly defines `key_encrypted` column. The prior wiped build used bytea per OBSERVATION. 

Decision: keep table column `key_encrypted bytea not null` + `key_iv bytea not null` for AES-256-GCM, and provide SQL functions using **pgcrypto** (`encrypt`/`decrypt` with `aes` cipher, `'aes-gcm'`?) — pgcrypto supports `encrypt(data, key, 'aes')` but GCM not in pgcrypto (pgcrypto has `aes-cbc/pgp` only; GCM is via extension `pgcrypto`? No — GCM is not supported by pgcrypto; it supports pgp, aes-cbc/ecb, bf, etc.). The prior build used a custom `bytea` type only. 

Simplest defensible MVP: use pgcrypto PGP symmetric with app-level key stored in supabase `vault` (create_secret / decrypted_secrets). parts.text:
Key finding: `packages/ui/src` imports `ExecutionStatus` type from `@aevryn/db/domain`. So my new db package MUST export a `domain` module with an `ExecutionStatus` type. Hmm — but the new schema has `RunStatus` (run_status) with values `pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled`. The old `ExecutionStatus` was `pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled` — EXACTLY the same value set as new `RunStatus`! So old ExecutionStatus ≈ new RunStatus. 

The ui components use `ExecutionStatus` for thread/run status badges (running/paused etc.). To keep ui typechecking green (and meaningful), I should provide `ExecutionStatus` as a type. Options:
1. Export `RunStatus` and alias `ExecutionStatus = RunStatus` in domain.ts. But wait — does the new domain include "paused"? RunStatus: pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled (no paused). Old ExecutionStatus also had no "paused" but sidebar likely uses paused/pending/... let me check ui usage: how does sidebar-menu use ExecutionStatus? Probably `status: ExecutionStatus` mapped to dot color. If I alias ExecutionStatus = RunStatus, ui stays type-compatible. But semantics: ui sidebar shows run status of threads. Fine.

Actually, cleaner: the plan docs define run_status (values above). The old ExecutionStatus had values `pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled`. Let me look at the exact old domain.ts: EXECUTION_STATUSES = [... "pending","running","sleeping","waiting","awaiting_approval","completed","failed","cancelled"]. The new run_status enum per SCHEMA.md = "pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled". Identical sets! Great — alias `ExecutionStatus` → `RunStatus` union, semantically an execution is a run in the new model. I'll export both names (RunStatus canonical, ExecutionStatus as deprecated alias) so ui imports work unchanged.

Do I want to verify ui typechecks after? ui imports ExecutionStatus from @aevryn/db/domain — as long as domains export it, ui compiles. But ui also imports @aevryn/config tsconfig base — which I'm restoring. ui package.json deps include @aevryn/db — restored. So ui should typecheck again. Good sign to also run check-types for ui.

Now, do I keep `@aevryn/ui` exporting path "./../@aevryn/db/domain"? Actually the import is `from "@aevryn/db/domain"` — my db package must have exports map `"./domain": "./src/domain.ts"` (like before: `"./*": "./src/*.ts"`). Good.

Now let me check side effects of `ExecutionStatus` usage: grep the two ui files to see what statuses they reference (whether "paused"/"idle" appear). If they use literal "paused" which isn't in RunStatus, typecheck breaks. Let me check.

Also decide: keep deps set matching old db package.json minus @aevryn/env + zod (keep zod actually? not needed; but catalog has it... I'll keep minimal: dotenv, drizzle-orm, pg; dev: @aevryn/config, @types/pg, drizzle-kit, tsx, typescript, ulid). Also `postgres` lib was in old; unused for our purposes — drop. Keep reset.ts.

Also root package.json references `@aevryn/config` devDep — resolved once restored. Good.

Now: bun install will fail until all workspace-deps in manifests resolve? We restore @aevryn/config + @aevryn/db. Remaining broken refs: apps/web → @aevryn/api, @aevryn/auth, @aevryn/inngest, @aevryn/workflow. These packages are being deleted (staged). So `bun install` will error "package not found in workspace" — need to trim apps/web package.json deps. Unless bun tolerates it. I expect it fails. I'll trim apps/web package.json minimal: remove the 4 dead @aevryn/* deps + @trpc/client, @trpc/server, @trpc/tanstack-react-query, better-auth (all now unused since api/auth removed). Keep rest. That's necessary for install; acceptable minimal scope.

Wait — but apps/web has source files that import those packages: src/utils/trpc.ts (imports trpc client + api router), src/lib/evlog-auth.ts (imports @aevryn/auth), src/app/api/auth/...route.ts (imports @aevryn/auth), src/app/api/trpc/[...]/route.ts (imports @aevryn/api), src/app/api/inngest/route.ts (imports @aevryn/inngest), src/app/api/v1/hooks/[token]/route.ts (imports @aevryn/workflow probably). Deleting the packages breaks apps/web typecheck (tsc --noEmit). spme of those files import from removed packages. If I remove the deps, apps/web source won't resolve imports → heavier breakage than expected. But apps/web is ALREADY broken (deps missing). For next dev to run, these files break at import time.

Do I need apps/web to run for commit 3? No. Verification = db schema. But making the whole monorepo happy requires removing/replacing those app files — which belongs to auth (P1) & api-refactor (P3) commits. The user said keep codebase as-is. Commit 3 shouldn't rewrite apps/web. 

Resolution: Leave apps/web manifests + source untouched for now. For `bun install` to succeed, I need to test whether bun errors on missing workspace deps. If it errors, I have two options: (a) trim apps/web deps (files that import them break equally whether dep exists or not — they currently DON'T exist, so nothing changes for the worse; removing the manifest entries makes install succeed while src files still fail typecheck — same red status). Button: removing manifest entries is safe & strictly reduces breakage (bundler resolves missing module at build/dev time anyway). 

Actually — wait. Let me reconsider: maybe `bun install` does NOT fail on missing workspace deps. Some bun versions just skip them or leave them unresolved with a warning. Let me just try it after adding config+db. If it works, leave apps/web alone entirely. If it fails, trim the 4 deps + trpc/better-auth.

I think that's the right call — minimal, only fix what blocks the db work.

Let me now check the two ui files to see the ExecutionStatus usage (statuses referenced).

Then I'll write all files. Let me plan the concrete file list:

**packages/config/**
- package.json: name @aevryn/config, private, version 0.0.0, exports "./tsconfig.base.json": "./tsconfig.base.json", files ["tsconfig.base.json"]. Old config was just tsconfig.base.json. package.json probably `{ "name": "@aevryn/config", "files": ["tsconfig.base.json"] }`. Since TS extends "@aevryn/config/tsconfig.base.json" resolves via exports map.
- tsconfig.base.json: strict options + paths alias `@/*` → `src/*` + moduleResolution bundler, target ESNext, module ESNext, etc. Minimal: 
```
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ESNext",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "paths": { "@/*": ["src/*"] }
  }
}
```
But env/ui tsconfigs extend and override (ui sets jsx, lib, types, declaration). Old base had strict etc. Fine.

Wait — db tsconfig old overrode with noEmit? No, it set declaration/declarationMap/sourceMap/outDir dist/composite. But root-level check-types uses `tsc --noEmit` per package scripts? ui has `check-types: tsc --noEmit`. For db, old package had no check-types script; but db scripts were db:* only. I'll add check-types script to db package for verification (tsc --noEmit). But db tsconfig sets composite → tsc --noEmit conflicts with composite (composite requires emit). Simplest: db tsconfig WITHOUT composite; keep declaration false; just strict typecheck. The old one had composite for build (dist). Since nothing imports db compiled output (workspace uses TS source via exports "./src/*.ts"), noEmit is fine. I'll set db tsconfig to extend base (noEmit true) + include schema. That satisfies `tsc --noEmit`. Drop composite/outDir (no build needed for a source-exported package). Cleaner.

**packages/db/**
- package.json (name @aevryn/db, exports "." and ".*")
- tsconfig.json (extends config, include src)
- drizzle.config.ts (dotenv from ../../apps/web/.env, schema ./src/schema/index.ts, out ./src/migrations, dialect postgresql)

--- packages/agent/src/capabilities/schedule-create.ts	
+++ packages/agent/src/capabilities/schedule-create.ts	
@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+import { computeNextRun, WorkflowService } from "@aevryn/workflow";
+import { z } from "zod";
+
+import type { Capability } from "../capability";
+import { toCapabilityFailure } from "../errors";
+
+const createScheduleInputSchema = z
+	.object({
+		cron: z
+			.string()
+			.min(1)
+			.max(100)
+			.describe(
+				"Standard 5-field cron expression (minute hour day month weekday), e.g. '0 9 * * 1' for weekly Monday 9am.",
+			)
+			.optional(),
+		intervalSeconds: z
+			.number()
+			.int()
+			.positive()
+			.max(86_400)
+			.describe("Fixed interval in seconds between runs (max 24 hours).")
+			.optional(),
+		prompt: z
+			.string()
+			.min(1)
+			.max(2000)
+			.optional()
+			.describe(
+				"Specific instruction to run at each fire. Defaults to the workflow objective.",
+			),
+		startAt: z
+			.string()
+			.datetime({ offset: true })
+			.optional()
+			.describe(
+				"Optional first run time as an ISO-8601 timestamp (e.g. '2026-09-15T09:00:00Z'); defaults to now.",
+			),
+	})
+	.superRefine((value, ctx) => {
+		if (!value.cron && !value.intervalSeconds) {
+			ctx.addIssue({
+				code: "custom",
+				path: ["cron"],
+				message: "Provide either cron or intervalSeconds.",
+			});
+		}
+	});
+
+export function createScheduleCapability(
+	workflowId: string,
+	userId: string,
+): Capability {
+	const service = new WorkflowService();
+	return {
+		name: "createSchedule",
+		description:
+			"Create a recurring schedule on this workflow. The workflow runs " +
+			"again automatically at each scheduled time (cron expression or fixed " +
+			"interval), letting you monitor something over time and report back. " +
+			"Use this for 'check every ...', 'monitor ... until ...', or 'notify me " +
+			"when ...' objectives instead of finishing immediately.",
+		inputSchema: createScheduleInputSchema,
+		async execute(input) {
+			const parsed = createScheduleInputSchema.safeParse(input);
+			if (!parsed.success) {
+				return {
+					ok: false,
+					error: {
+						code: "INVALID_CAPABILITY_INPUT",
+						message: parsed.error.message,
+						failureClass: "fatal",
+						retryable: false,
+					},
+				};
+			}
+			try {
+				const startDate = parsed.data.startAt
+					? new Date(parsed.data.startAt)
+					: undefined;
+				const nextRunAt = computeNextRun(
+					parsed.data.cron,
+					parsed.data.intervalSeconds,
+					startDate,
+				);
+				const schedule = await service.createSchedule({
+					userId,
+					workflowId,
+					cron: parsed.data.cron,
+					intervalSeconds: parsed.data.intervalSeconds,
+					startAt: startDate,
+					config: { prompt: parsed.data.prompt },
+				});
+				return {
+					ok: true,
+					data: {
+						scheduleId: schedule.id,
+						cron: schedule.cron,
+						intervalSeconds: schedule.intervalSeconds,
+						prompt: parsed.data.prompt,
+						nextRunAt: nextRunAt.toISOString(),
+					},
+				};
+			} catch (error) {
+				return toCapabilityFailure(error, 0);
+			}
+		},
+	};
+}

+import { monotonicFactory } from "ulid";
+
+const factory = monotonicFactory();
+
+export const ID_PREFIXES = {
+	workflow: "wf_",
+	execution: "exe_",
+	step: "step_",
+	tool: "tool_",
+	observation: "obs_",
+	recovery: "rec_",
+	memory: "mem_",
+	event: "evt_",
+	agentState: "agent_state_",
+	schedule: "sched_",
+	notification: "ntf_",
+	webhook: "whk_",
+	approval: "ap_",
+} as const;
+
+export type IdPrefix = (typeof ID_PREFIXES)[keyof typeof ID_PREFIXES];
+
+export function makeId(prefix: IdPrefix): string {
+	return `${prefix}${factory()}`;
+}
+
+export function isValidId(prefix: IdPrefix, id: string): boolean {
+	if (!id.startsWith(prefix)) return false;
+	return /^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$/.test(id.slice(prefix.length));
+}
+
+export const ids = {
+	workflow: () => makeId(ID_PREFIXES.workflow),
+	execution: () => makeId(ID_PREFIXES.execution),
+	step: () => makeId(ID_PREFIXES.step),
+	tool: () => makeId(ID_PREFIXES.tool),
+	observation: () => makeId(ID_PREFIXES.observation),
+	recovery: () => makeId(ID_PREFIXES.recovery),
+	memory: () => makeId(ID_PREFIXES.memory),

+
